Horn clauses and Datalog

Source: vignettes/horn.Rmd
horn.Rmd
library(z3r)
ctx <- z3_context()
I <- z3_int_sort(ctx)
B <- z3_bool_sort(ctx)

Z3’s fixedpoint engine answers reachability questions over recursively defined relations. With finite relations this is Datalog. With arithmetic and other theories it solves constrained Horn clauses (CHC), the form that many program verification problems take: “can this program reach an error state?”. The Spacer engine either finds a derivation (a counterexample) or an inductive invariant (a proof).

A loop that never reaches 7 

x := 0
while (*) x := x + 2
assert(x != 7)

The reachable values of x form a relation inv:

inv <- z3_function(ctx, "inv", I, B)
x <- z3_int(ctx, "x")
fp <- z3_fixedpoint(ctx)
z3_register_relation(fp, inv)
z3_add_rule(fp, inv(0), name = "init")
z3_add_rule(fp, z3_forall(x, z3_implies(inv(x), inv(x + 2))), name = "step")
z3_query(fp, z3_exists(x, inv(x) & x == 7))
#> [1] "unsat"

"unsat": 7 is not reachable. The answer is an invariant that proves it:

z3_answer(fp)
#> <z3_expr Bool> (forall ((A Int))
#>   (! (= (inv A)
#>         (and (not (= A 7))
#>              (not (= A 5))
#>              (not (= A 3))
#>              (not (= A 1))
#>              (not (<= A (- 1)))))
#>      :weight 0))

8 is reachable, and the answer is the derivation:

z3_query(fp, z3_exists(x, inv(x) & x == 8))
#> [1] "sat"
z3_answer_rule_names(fp)
#> [1] "<null>;step;step;step;step;init"

A two-variable program 

x := 0; y := 0
while (*) { x := x + 1; y := y + 2 }
assert(y == 2 * x)
y <- z3_int(ctx, "y")
x2 <- z3_int(ctx, "x2")
y2 <- z3_int(ctx, "y2")
loop <- z3_function(ctx, "loop", list(I, I), B)
fp <- z3_fixedpoint(ctx)
z3_register_relation(fp, loop)
z3_add_rule(fp, loop(0, 0))
z3_add_rule(fp, z3_forall(list(x, y, x2, y2),
  z3_implies(loop(x, y) & x2 == x + 1 & y2 == y + 2, loop(x2, y2))))
z3_query(fp, z3_exists(list(x, y), loop(x, y) & y != 2 * x))
#> [1] "unsat"
z3_answer(fp)
#> <z3_expr Bool> (forall ((A Int) (B Int))
#>   (! (= (loop A B)
#>         (and (not (<= (+ (* 2 A) (* (- 1) B)) (- 1)))
#>              (not (>= (+ (* 2 A) (* (- 1) B)) 1))))
#>      :weight 0))

Datalog

With the Datalog engine and finite domains, relations are computed bottom-up:

N <- z3_finite_domain_sort(ctx, "Node", 16)
edge <- z3_function(ctx, "edge", list(N, N), B)
path <- z3_function(ctx, "path", list(N, N), B)
a <- z3_const(ctx, "a", N)
b <- z3_const(ctx, "b", N)
c <- z3_const(ctx, "c", N)
fp <- z3_fixedpoint(ctx)
z3_set_params(fp, engine = "datalog")
z3_register_relation(fp, edge)
z3_register_relation(fp, path)
for (e in list(c(1, 2), c(2, 3), c(3, 4), c(5, 6))) z3_add_fact(fp, edge, e)
z3_add_rule(fp, z3_forall(list(a, b), z3_implies(edge(a, b), path(a, b))))
z3_add_rule(fp, z3_forall(list(a, b, c), z3_implies(edge(a, b) & path(b, c), path(a, c))))
z3_query(fp, path)
#> [1] "sat"
z3_answer(fp)
#> <z3_expr Bool> (or (and (= (:var 0) 1) (= (:var 1) 2))
#>     (and (= (:var 0) 2) (= (:var 1) 3))
#>     (and (= (:var 0) 3) (= (:var 1) 4))
#>     (and (= (:var 0) 5) (= (:var 1) 6))
#>     (and (= (:var 0) 1) (= (:var 1) 3))
#>     (and (= (:var 0) 2) (= (:var 1) 4))
#>     (and (= (:var 0) 1) (= (:var 1) 4)))

Model-based projection

Spacer’s building blocks are available on their own. Model-based projection removes variables from a formula, guided by a model: the result holds in the model and implies the formula with the variables existentially quantified. Here the model has x = 3, y = 4, and projecting x out of x > 2 & y == x + 1 leaves a constraint on y:

x <- z3_int(ctx, "x")
y <- z3_int(ctx, "y")
f <- x > 2 & y == x + 1
sol <- z3_solver(ctx)
z3_add(sol, f)
z3_check(sol)
#> [1] "sat"
m <- z3_model(sol)
z3_model_project(m, x, f)
#> <z3_expr Bool> (not (<= y 3))
w <- z3_model_project(m, x, f, method = "witness")
w$formula
#> <z3_expr Bool> (and (>= y 4))
w$terms
#> [[1]]
#> <z3_expr Int> (+ (- 1) y)

The witness says how to recover x from y. z3_model_extrapolate() generalizes the model into a conjunction of literals that implies a formula, and z3_qe_lite() eliminates the variables that cheap rewriting can remove:

z3_model_extrapolate(m, f | y < 0)
#> <z3_expr Bool> (and (= y (+ x 1)) (> x 2))
z3_qe_lite(x, f)
#> $formula
#> <z3_expr Bool> (> (+ (- 1) y) 2)
#> 
#> $remaining
#> list()

More

  • z3_fixedpoint_rules(), z3_param_help(fp), z3_statistics(fp).
  • Spacer: z3_ground_answer(), z3_answer_trace(), z3_add_invariant(), z3_reachable(), z3_cover() and z3_add_cover(); z3_query(fp, q, level = k) starts the search at level k.
  • Rules in SMT-LIB2 Horn format can be given to a solver created with z3_solver(ctx, logic = "HORN").
